evidence_items.explanation: This is direct evidence of organized opposition to broad AI mandates. The same paper supports existing consumer-protection enforcement and court remedies, so its position is narrower than rejecting every substantive legal safeguard.

evidence_items.publisher: Reason; Robin Hanson and Ronald Bailey
evidence_items.explanation: Hanson publicly opposes additional AI regulation, but also accepts regulation comparable to that applied to people performing similar roles. Bailey's opposing contribution favors restrictions on government facial-recognition surveillance, illustrating disagreement within the same publication.

The paper advocates a permissive default and warns against highly restrictive regulation. It confirms sustained advocacy, but is not independent evidence of the number or influence of actors sharing that position.

unresolved_gaps: The records establish examples of opposition but not its prevalence or comparative concentration among libertarian technology actors.
